title: Memory Needs Checks, Harnesses Need Gates
description: Expectation-grounded memory, guarded harness updates, asynchronous agent RL, and benchmarks for efficiency and autonomous AI development.
lead: This selection treats agent improvement as an evaluation problem. Procedural memory needs expectation checks and utility-based pruning, harness changes need retention gates, and self-improvement results need randomized task order. New training and benchmark results add evidence on asynchronous RL, trajectory efficiency, autonomous AI development, and judge calibration.
chat_summary_ru:
Главная тема: память и самоизменение агентов полезны только при строгой проверке. AdMem решает 441 задачу против 388 у ReAct, а наивная память между задачами часто ухудшает результат.
Для изменений обвязки агента предлагают проверять текущий прогресс, сохранение прошлых навыков и корректность перед принятием изменения.
Перед оценкой цикла памяти перемешивайте порядок задач, а автоматические судьи калибруйте по реальным исходам.

items.title: AdMem: Expectation-Grounded Procedural Memory
items.take: AdMem turns expectation checks into utility-ranked procedural memories without requiring an environment reward.
points: Before each action, the actor commits to an expected outcome, while a concurrent critic compares the realized outcome and writes a binary reward and reflection.
A scalar utility updated online under a noisy-OR reward model ranks retrieval with context similarity and controls eviction and merging.
Across 707 tasks in eight AgentBoard domains, AdMem solved 441 tasks, versus 388 for ReAct and 312 for workflow induction.
Workflow-induction memory underperformed memoryless ReAct in seven of eight domains, and an unstructured per-step store lost half of ReAct's completions on Jericho.
items.adopt: When building an agent memory, write entries only after an expectation check, rank them by utility and context similarity, and add utility-based eviction and merging.

items.title: Harness-Level Forgetting
items.take: Updating any harness component can break previously reliable behavior while leaving the model untouched.
points: The paper names this failure harness-level forgetting and provides a measurement protocol.
A Continual Optimizer proposes candidate harnesses from post-execution feedback, and a Continual Evaluator commits only after checking current improvement, historical retention, and validity.

Experiments on textual reasoning, multimodal perception, and open-world interaction show capability accumulation and failure recovery, with relative gains exceeding 10% over corresponding baselines in multiple settings.
items.adopt: Gate every harness change with an evaluator that checks historical retention alongside current improvement and validity before commit.

items.title: The Fragility of Self-Improving Agents
items.take: Noisy multi-step evaluation and hidden task curricula can make self-improvement results fragile.
points: Agent evaluation is inherently noisy in complex environments and on multi-step tasks, and a self-improving loop can amplify that noise.
Improvement depends heavily on task order, and prior work often uses default orderings that impose an implicit curriculum.
Detailed rubrics and environment feedback in memory construction partially close the performance degradation, but significant gaps remain.
items.adopt: Shuffle task order before measuring a memory loop, and test detailed rubrics plus environment feedback as memory inputs rather than assuming they remove degradation.

items.title: FlashREINFORCE: Single-Rollout Asynchronous RL
items.take: FlashREINFORCE combines critic-free, single-rollout asynchronous training with controls for policy drift and negative updates.
points: One-Batch REINFORCE, a Sequence Trust Region, and Sample-Mean Optimization provide prompt coverage and batch centering while controlling policy drift and length-amplified negative updates.
Training remained stable through 6,000 updates on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B at policy lag four, and through 1,450 updates on Qwen3-30B-A3B at lag eight.
With half the rollouts, it scored 38.0 versus 36.3 for published synchronous baselines on the Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B five-benchmark mean.
On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct it maintained tool use where GRPO stopped calling tools and reached 98.3% seen and 96.5% unseen ALFWorld success.
items.adopt: For asynchronous agent RL, evaluate single-rollout training with explicit drift and negative-update controls, and track tool calling alongside task success.

items.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
items.take: Singularity-Bench evaluates autonomous AI development across six end-to-end tasks and exposes reward hacking in the execution framework.
points: The tasks span pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration.
Red-teaming covered 9 of the 10 categories in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, exposed reward-hacking vulnerabilities in Harbor, and led to Breakwater.
Opus 5.5 with Claude Code matched or outperformed the human baseline on all six tasks with a Singularity-Index of 1.25, while the remaining agents averaged 0.58.
items.adopt: Use end-to-end agent-building tasks to evaluate autonomous development, and red-team the execution framework for reward hacking before trusting scores.

items.title: DetourBench: Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
items.take: DetourBench makes trajectory efficiency measurable by computing exact minimum action counts for partially observable tasks.
points: Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery, allowing exhaustive search to compute the exact minimum action count.
Across 375 scored episodes from five model endpoints on 25 integrated tasks with three repeats, success ranged from 58.7% to 96.0%.
items.adopt: Benchmark interactive agents with both success and distance from an exact minimum-action bound so efficient trajectories are distinguishable from successful detours.

items.title: ReproBridge and AutoRefine
items.take: Refined reproduction artifacts and calibrated judges improve both paper reproduction and agreement with deployed agent outcomes.
points: On 1,029 tasks from 36 papers, refined artifacts in ReproBridge raised reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% across four models and cut API spending by 19.7%.
On Meta's deployed performance-optimization agent, AutoRefine judge calibration raised agreement between the judge and real outcomes from 0.16 to 0.51.
items.adopt: Refine reproduction artifacts before execution and calibrate agent judges against real outcomes before using their scores for optimization.

adopt_summary: Store procedural memories only after expectation checks, with utility-based retrieval and eviction.
Gate harness changes on current improvement, historical retention, and validity.
Shuffle task order before evaluating memory or self-improvement loops.
Evaluate agents on trajectory efficiency, tool use, and reward hacking, not success alone.
Calibrate automated judges against real outcomes.
